title: Collection and Post-Surgical Excision of Human Kidney Tissue
author: Maya Brewer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.buggnttw
materials: Receive excised kidney from full nephrectomy.

steps.title: Select eligible kidney tissue
steps.instruction: Choose kidney specimens from patients younger than 65 years who have provided consent for research use.

steps.title: Halve kidney and open
steps.instruction: Cut the kidney in half along its longest plane and open the halves like a book.

steps.title: Excise distal tissue block
steps.instruction: Cut out a portion of the kidney measuring approximately 80 × 60 × 4 mm that is farthest away from the tumor location.

steps.title: Photograph excised piece
steps.instruction: Take a picture of the smaller excised piece, showing its original location within the whole kidney if possible.

steps.title: Section into smaller pieces
steps.instruction: Cut the excised piece into about four rectangular fragments, each roughly 2 × 15 × 4 mm.

steps.title: Image each fragment
steps.instruction: Capture images of each small fragment, noting its original position in the kidney.

steps.title: Store tissue on ice
steps.instruction: Place the tissue fragments in a plastic container on ice, then hand the container to personnel responsible for long‑term storage.

substeps.instruction: Place fragments in a plastic container kept on ice.
Transfer the container to the team preparing tissue for long‑term storage.
